sources.title: Review of the Department of Justice’s Planning and Implementation of Its Zero Tolerance Policy and Its Coordination with the Departments of Homeland Security and Health and Human Services

reason: The primary DOJ OIG report directly documents the May 11 call and attributes the statement to Sessions. The entry’s 'Trump:' prefix is not supported: the report describes Sessions, not Donald Trump, as the speaker.

No credible source located in this run directly documents Stephen Miller telling the Justice Department on May 14, 2018 to increase child separation. Sources document Miller’s broader role in immigration policy, but not this exact dated instruction.

A June 18, 2020 report citing John Bolton’s forthcoming memoir said Trump told Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin to “go after bitcoin” in May 2018, but it did not establish May 15 as the date. The available account is retrospective and does not provide solid direct evidence for this exact dated entry.

sources.title: New York Attorney General Sues Trump Foundation After 2-Year Investigation

supported_event_claim: On June 14, 2018, New York Attorney General Barbara Underwood filed a lawsuit against the Donald J. Trump Foundation and its directors. The complaint alleged violations of New York charity law, including alleged self-dealing and unlawful political coordination; the allegations were claims in the filing, not a finding of guilt at that time.
reason: The contemporaneous New York Times report identifies the filing date and allegations; the New York Attorney General later officially confirmed that the lawsuit had been filed in June 2018.

sources.title: Epstein appeared to offer political advice on dealing with Trump in 2018: Emails

supported_event_claim: ABC News reported that released emails show Jeffrey Epstein wrote to Council of Europe Secretary General Thorbjørn Jagland on June 24, 2018, suggesting that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov could gain insight by talking with Epstein; Epstein also wrote that former Russian diplomat Vitaly Churkin understood Trump after conversations with Epstein.
reason: The event date is the date in the email, while the available report was published years later (2025-11-14) after release of the records. This supports the existence and wording of the correspondence, not Epstein's claimed influence or any allegation about Russian intelligence.

sources.title: GOP Congressmen Visit Moscow, Thaw Icy Relations Before Trump-Putin Talks

supported_event_claim: A Republican congressional delegation visited Moscow around the 2018 Fourth of July, including Senator Richard Shelby and other Republican lawmakers; the trip was described as the first congressional delegation to Russia since its annexation of Crimea.
reason: NPR contemporaneously reported the delegation’s Moscow visit on July 4, 2018, and Senator Thune’s official statement confirmed the trip and meetings with U.S. and Russian officials. The sources establish a congressional delegation trip, not a trip by Trump himself.

sources.title: Grand Jury Indicts 12 Russian Intelligence Officers for Hacking Offenses Related to the 2016 Election

sources.title: Russia still working to undermine U.S. elections, top national security officials warn

supported_event_claim: At an August 2, 2018 White House briefing, senior U.S. national-security and intelligence officials warned that Russia was conducting ongoing, pervasive efforts to interfere in the 2018 midterm elections.
reason: NBC's contemporaneous report identifies the briefing participants and quotes DNI Director Dan Coats and FBI Director Christopher Wray. This supports the warning, without adopting any unsupported claim about motive or effectiveness.

sources.title: U.S. Senator Paul delivers letter from Trump to Putin's government

supported_event_claim: Sen. Rand Paul said on August 8, 2018 that he had delivered a letter from President Donald Trump to the Russian government during Paul's Moscow visit; the White House characterized it as a letter of introduction provided at Paul's request.
reason: Reuters directly reports Paul's statement, the White House's characterization, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov's confirmation that a Trump letter had been delivered. The assigned date (2018-08-06) differs from Reuters' publication date (2018-08-08); the article describes the delivery during Paul's visit rather than establishing August 6 as the delivery date.

sources.title: Steve Bannon trying to get on disgraced Jeffrey Epstein's good side

reason: The contemporaneous report directly describes the observed entry and identifies the location and timing. It does not establish that the meeting was secret in the strong sense implied by the entry, nor does it establish speculation about purpose or motive.

sources.title: The Day Jeffrey Epstein Told Me He Had Dirt on Powerful People

supported_event_claim: In an August 2018 interview, Epstein told journalist James B. Stewart he had been advising Tesla; Tesla denied such contact.

Available documents do not directly establish the claimed August 2018 strategy consultation between Epstein and Ken Starr specifically to protect Trump; communications or later representation alone cannot support that motive.

The official Federal Register record verifies that Trump signed Executive Order 13848 on September 12, 2018, concerning sanctions for foreign interference in a U.S. election (published September 14), but it provides no evidence that he was tricked into signing it. No credible direct source for the exact 'tricked' claim was found.

No credible government record or reputable original reporting located in this run supports the specific claim that Senator Leahy said the U.S. Senate belonged to the Trump White House on September 28, 2018. sources.title: Assessment of the Saudi Government’s Role in the Killing of Jamal Khashoggi
sources.publisher: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

supported_event_claim: Jamal Khashoggi was killed in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul on October 2, 2018. A declassified U.S. intelligence assessment said Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman approved an operation to capture or kill him; Saudi authorities rejected that assessment.
reason: The underlying killing is directly documented, and the ODNI assessment supports the attributed approval claim. The wording 'has ... assassinated' is stronger than the publicly established record, so the claim is narrowed to the documented killing and the U.S. intelligence assessment, with Saudi denial noted. Reuters’ URL is dated February 27, 2021, while its dateline and the ODNI document date are February 26, 2021.

No credible direct source located supports the specific claim that National Security Adviser John Bolton stopped the Department of Homeland Security from combating white supremacy on October 4, 2018. sources.title: China grants 18 trademarks in 2 months to Trump, daughter

No solid direct source was found for the exact composite claim that Trump began covering for Mohammed bin Salman on 2018-10-15 because of a $100 million payment and pleas from Israel and Egypt. The Washington Post report that was located says the United States received the Saudi payment on Tuesday, 2018-10-16 (not October 15), and reports the payment's stated Syria-stabilization purpose; it does not establish that it caused Trump's position or that Israel and Egypt made the alleged pleas.

sources.title: Trump: 'This was an anti-Semitic attack at its worst'

'White nationalist' is a characterization of the attacker/ideology in the entry, not wording established as Trump's statement by this source, so the claim is narrowed and attributed neutrally.
